name: Krios 5 Cryo-TEM

specs.Data handling: On-the-fly motion correction and EER 8K decoding
specs.Throughput: Up to 25% faster than the previous generation (manufacturer claim)
specs.Calibration: Magnification calibration accuracy within 1% for single-particle analysis

summary: The current generation of Thermo Fisher's high-end Krios cryo-transmission electron microscope (the former Krios G4 product page now leads to it), used for atomic-resolution single-particle analysis and cryo-electron tomography in shared cryo-EM facilities.

name: Glacios 3 Cryo-TEM

specs.Installation: READY System to reduce infrastructure requirements

summary: A 200 kV cryo-TEM that sits between screening microscopes and the 300 kV Krios, used for sample screening and for single-particle data collection in labs without a full high-end facility. The Glacios 3 is the current version of the Glacios line.

name: Tundra Cryo-TEM

resolution.note: Manufacturer example: biological single-particle reconstructions down to 2.1 Å at 100 kV

specs.Detector: Integrated Falcon C direct electron detector

summary: A compact 100 kV cryo-TEM intended to make single-particle cryo-EM accessible to individual labs, with automated grid loading and an integrated direct electron detector.

name: Talos L120C

specs.Cameras: Ceta-F; optional Falcon C direct electron detector

summary: A 120 kV transmission electron microscope for routine imaging of stained biological sections and negative-stain or cryo samples, often used for sample screening.

name: Talos F200C

specs.STEM: Up to four-channel integrated STEM detectors, EDS options

summary: A 200 kV field-emission TEM used for both materials and life-science work, including cryo-EM with a direct electron detector and STEM with EDS analysis.

name: Spectra Ultra

resolution.note: STEM resolution <50 pm at 300 kV, probe+image corrected (X-FEG/Mono or UltiMono); information limit <60 pm

specs.Corrector: S-CORR probe corrector; probe+image corrected configurations
specs.Detectors: Panther 16-segment STEM detection; EMPAD 4D-STEM (128 x 128 px, 1,100 fps); Ceta camera

summary: An aberration-corrected scanning/transmission electron microscope for atomic-resolution materials science, with a very large solid-angle X-ray detector for elemental mapping and a wide range of accelerating voltages for beam-sensitive samples.

name: Aquilos 2 Cryo-FIB

specs.Automation: AutoTEM Cryo batch lamella milling; AutoScript; Auto Slice & View
specs.Options: iFLM integrated fluorescence microscope; EasyLift NanoManipulator for cryo lift-out; integrated sputter coater

summary: A cryo focused-ion-beam SEM that mills thin lamellae out of frozen cells and tissues so they can be imaged by cryo-electron tomography. An optional built-in fluorescence microscope helps target the milling to labelled structures.

name: Arctis Cryo-PFIB

specs.Autoloader: Robotic loader for up to 12 vitrified grids; transfer to Krios/Glacios in a vacuum capsule

summary: An automated cryo plasma-FIB for preparing lamellae from vitrified samples on many grids in one run, with an autoloader shared with Thermo Fisher cryo-TEMs and an integrated fluorescence microscope for targeting.

name: Hydra Bio Plasma-FIB
summary: A plasma focused-ion-beam SEM for life science whose ion species can be switched, used for serial-milling volume EM and for preparing cryo-tomography lamellae.

name: Helios 5 DualBeam

specs.Imaging: Sub-nm SEM and STEM imaging (manufacturer claim)

summary: A gallium-ion focused-ion-beam SEM, the flagship of Thermo Fisher's Ga DualBeam range, used for TEM sample preparation and for slice-and-view 3D imaging.

name: Apreo 2 SEM

resolution.note: Apreo 2 S at 1 kV; 0.8 nm at 500 V with beam deceleration

specs.Detectors (2 S): ETD, T1, T2, T3 in-lens, IR-CCD, Nav-Cam+; options include DBS, STEM 3+, EDS, EBSD

summary: A field-emission SEM with in-lens detectors and beam deceleration for high-resolution imaging at low landing energy. It is offered as S and C variants and serves as the companion platform for Volumescope 2 serial block-face imaging.
applications: Low-kV imaging of biological and materials samples

name: Volumescope 2 SEM

specs.Principle: Serial block-face SEM: in situ sectioning and imaging of resin-embedded tissue
specs.Other modes: Large-area 2D imaging, array tomography, STEM, cryo-SEM, CLEM, EDS

summary: A serial block-face SEM system that repeatedly cuts and images a resin-embedded tissue block to build a 3D stack of ultrastructure.

name: CRYO ARM 300 II (JEM-3300)
summary: JEOL's 300 kV cryo-EM with a cold field emission gun and an in-column Omega energy filter, announced in January 2021 with about twice the throughput of the original CRYO ARM 300.

sources.title: JEOL USA press release: CRYO ARM 300 II (JEM-3300)

name: JEM-1400Flash

resolution.note: Lattice resolution, high-resolution (HR) pole piece; 0.2 nm with high-contrast (HC) pole piece

summary: A 120 kV TEM aimed at biology, with a sensitive sCMOS camera, large-area montaging, and an overlay tool for correlating light-microscope images. JEOL lists it as discontinued.

name: JEM-ARM300F2 (GRAND ARM 2)

resolution.note: STEM resolution 53 pm at 300 kV with FHP2 pole piece and Cs corrector; 96 pm at 80 kV

specs.Accelerating voltage: 300 kV and 80 kV standard (40-200 kV also specified)
specs.TEM information limit: 60 pm non-linear, 90 pm linear (300 kV, FHP2)

summary: An aberration-corrected 300 kV atomic-resolution (S)TEM with a cold field emission gun. Its FHP2 pole piece is designed to combine very high spatial resolution with efficient X-ray collection.

name: JSM-IT800

resolution.note: SHL and i variants at 15 kV; 0.7 nm at 1 kV

specs.Variants: HL, i, is, SHL, SHLs (different objective lenses)
specs.Probe current: Up to 300-500 nA at 30 kV depending on variant

summary: A field-emission SEM offered with several objective-lens options for general-purpose, ultra-high-resolution or semiconductor work. JEOL lists it as discontinued.

name: HT7800
summary: A 120 kV TEM for biological and materials samples whose objective lens switches between a high-contrast mode for stained biological sections and a high-resolution mode.

name: SU8200 series (SU8220/SU8230/SU8240)

resolution.note: Secondary-electron resolution at 15 kV; 1.1 nm at 1 kV

specs.Electron gun: Cold field emission with 'mild flashing' for stable emission

summary: A cold-field-emission SEM series introduced in 2013 whose redesigned gun kept emission stable while preserving the high brightness of cold field emitters, giving sub-nanometre resolution at 15 kV.

name: GeminiSEM 360 / 460 / 560

specs.Low-kV: Sub-1 nm resolution below 1 kV without an immersion lens (560)
specs.Detectors: Inlens SE and energy-selective Inlens BSE, annular BSE, dual EDS ports

summary: A family of field-emission SEMs built around ZEISS's Gemini column, which keeps magnetic fields at the sample low so that magnetic samples and low-voltage imaging work well.

name: Crossbeam 350 / 550 / 750

specs.Workflows: 3D tomography, serial sectioning, TEM lamella preparation

summary: ZEISS's FIB-SEM line, combining a Gemini SEM column with a focused ion beam for serial-sectioning 3D imaging and TEM sample preparation; an optional laser removes large volumes quickly to reach buried regions.

name: MultiSEM 706

specs.Beams: 91 parallel electron beams in a hexagonal pattern
specs.Acquisition rate: >3 TB per hour; up to 1.22 gigapixels/s

summary: A multi-beam SEM that scans 91 electron beams in parallel, making it practical to image very large areas, such as thousands of serial brain sections for connectomics, at nanometre pixel sizes.

name: Xradia 620 Versa

resolution.note: Spatial resolution ~0.5 µm (ZEISS 2D target, 40x objective); 1.0 µm at 50 mm working distance ('resolution at a distance')

summary: A laboratory 3D X-ray microscope (micro-CT class) that reaches about 0.5 µm spatial resolution and keeps about 1 µm resolution with the sample 50 mm from the source.
applications: Non-destructive 3D imaging of materials, bone and tissue

sources.title: ZEISS product information: Xradia 610 and 620 Versa

name: Xradia 800 Ultra / 810 Ultra

resolution.note: Spatial resolution down to 50 nm; 16 nm voxel size

summary: A laboratory nanoscale X-ray microscope that uses X-ray optics to reach about 50 nm resolution in 3D, with Zernike phase contrast for weakly absorbing samples.
applications: Biological and soft samples with phase contrast

name: 3View

specs.Principle: Ultramicrotome inside the SEM chamber cuts the block face, then the fresh face is imaged

summary: The commercial version of serial block-face SEM: an ultramicrotome fitted inside an SEM chamber that alternately cuts and images a resin-embedded block, giving automated 3D ultrastructure of tissue.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Serial block-face scanning electron microscopy

name: Serial block-face SEM prototype
manufacturer: Denk lab (Max Planck Institute for Medical Research, Heidelberg)

specs.Sections: Stacks of several hundred sections, 50-70 nm thick

summary: Winfried Denk and Heinz Horstmann built an ultramicrotome into an SEM chamber and imaged each freshly cut block face, showing that axons and synapses could be traced through the resulting 3D stacks. The design became the basis for commercial serial block-face systems.

sources.title: Denk & Horstmann (2004) Serial block-face scanning electron microscopy to reconstruct three-dimensional tissue nanostructure. PLoS Biol 2:e329

name: Enhanced FIB-SEM
summary: A modified FIB-SEM developed at Janelia with improvements to reliability and control so that it can mill and image continuously for months, giving isotropic-voxel volumes large enough for whole-brain-region connectomics.

sources.title: Xu et al. (2017) Enhanced FIB-SEM systems for large-volume 3D imaging. eLife 6:e25916

name: Array tomography

specs.Sections: Ultrathin (50-200 nm) resin-embedded serial sections on glass slides

summary: Kristina Micheva and Stephen Smith introduced imaging ordered ribbons of ultrathin serial sections with repeated immunofluorescence staining and electron microscopy, giving many molecular labels plus ultrastructure in the same 3D volume.

sources.title: Micheva & Smith (2007) Array tomography: a new tool for imaging the molecular architecture and ultrastructure of neural circuits. Neuron 55:25-36

name: AMBER X 2
summary: A xenon plasma FIB-SEM for fast milling of large volumes, used for 3D tomography and TEM lamella preparation alongside multimodal analysis.

name: Dimension Icon

specs.Modes: PeakForce Tapping; ScanAsyst Plus self-optimizing imaging

summary: A large-sample, tip-scanning AFM with a 90 µm scan range and low drift, widely used in materials and surface-science labs.

name: NanoWizard V BioScience

specs.Speed: Fast scanning up to 400 lines/s (page also lists a 200 Hz option)
specs.Optical integration: Brightfield, DIC, confocal, TIRF and super-resolution microscopes; DirectOverlay
specs.Modes: PeakForce Tapping, QI, contact, tapping, force spectroscopy and mapping

summary: A BioAFM, originally from JPK, that mounts on inverted optical microscopes so cells and biomolecules can be imaged and mechanically probed while being viewed by fluorescence.

name: NanoWizard ULTRA Speed 3

specs.Optical integration: Mounted on inverted microscopes (e.g. Leica DMi8, Nikon Ti2, ZEISS LSM 800); compatible with STED and PALM/STORM
specs.Z: Structures up to 8 µm high with NestedScanner

summary: A fast-scanning BioAFM that combines video-like AFM imaging of biomolecular processes with simultaneous optical and super-resolution microscopy.

name: Cypher S

specs.Speed: 10-40x faster imaging than conventional AFMs (manufacturer claim)

summary: A compact, high-resolution AFM built for small fast cantilevers, used for atomic-scale imaging and quick scanning in air and liquid.
applications: High-resolution imaging of crystals and biomolecules

sources.title: Asylum Research: Cypher family of AFMs

name: Cypher VRS1250

specs.Frame rate: True video-rate imaging up to 45 frames/s

summary: The video-rate member of the Cypher AFM family, designed to follow dynamic processes such as protein assembly or crystal growth at up to 45 frames per second.

sources.title: Asylum Research: Cypher family of AFMs

name: NX10

specs.Scanner: Decoupled 2D flexure XY sample scanner and separate 1D flexure Z scanner
specs.Z: Out-of-axis motion <5 nm at full 15 µm extension

summary: A research AFM with separate XY and Z scanners, which keeps scans flat and orthogonal; its non-contact mode senses attractive van der Waals forces to protect tip and sample.

name: SS-NEX (Ando model)

specs.Standard scanner: 20 frames/s; XY 0.7 x 0.7 µm, Z 0.4 µm
specs.Wide scanner: 1 frame/s; XY 4 x 4 µm, Z 0.7 µm

summary: A sample-scanning high-speed AFM developed by Toshio Ando at Kanazawa University and commercialized by RIBM, used to film single protein molecules at work in liquid.

sources.title: RIBM: SS-NEX Ando model high-speed AFM

name: High-speed AFM for biomolecules
summary: Toshio Ando's group built an AFM with small cantilevers and fast scanners that captured images in tens of milliseconds. In 2010 they used it to film single myosin V molecules walking along actin, showing the motor's steps directly.

sources.title: Ando et al. (2001) A high-speed atomic force microscope for studying biological macromolecules. PNAS 98:12468
Kodera et al. (2010) Video imaging of walking myosin V by high-speed atomic force microscopy. Nature 468:72

name: SkyScan 1276 CMOS Edition

resolution.note: 6 µm spatial resolution (10% MTF); 2.8 µm smallest pixel size

specs.Object size: 75 mm diameter, 310 mm length (whole mouse or rat)

summary: A desktop in vivo micro-CT scanner for small animals, with low-dose fast scans and a dose estimate shown for each scan.

name: SkyScan 2214 CMOS Edition

resolution.note: <500 nm low-contrast resolution (10% MTF); 60 nm smallest pixel size

specs.Object size: Up to 300 mm diameter (140 mm scanning size), 400 mm length, 20 kg

summary: A floor-standing laboratory nano-CT system that reaches sub-micron 3D resolution on samples ranging from small specimens to large objects.

name: SXT-100

resolution.note: Lateral full-pitch resolution of about 50 nm

specs.Source: Laser-driven plasma soft X-ray source (water window)
specs.Sample: Vitrified cells; cryo stage at 100 K with vacuum load lock
specs.Tomography: Full tilt on capillaries or cryo lift-out pillars up to 10 µm

summary: A laboratory soft X-ray tomography microscope working in the 'water window', where carbon-rich organelles absorb strongly and water does not. It images whole frozen cells in 3D without stains, work that previously needed a synchrotron.

name: METEOR 2.0

specs.Integration: Cryo fluorescence microscope inside a cryo-FIB/SEM chamber
specs.Optics: High-NA objectives, high-QE camera, fast filter wheel
specs.Software: ODEMIS controls SEM, FIB, fluorescence and correlation

summary: A fluorescence microscope fitted into a cryo-FIB/SEM so that labelled targets can be located and checked during lamella milling without moving the sample between instruments.

name: THUNDER Imager EM Cryo CLEM

specs.Imaging: Widefield cryo fluorescence with THUNDER computational haze removal

summary: A cryo light microscope for locating fluorescent targets in vitrified samples before transfer to an electron microscope. It replaced the EM Cryo CLEM, and Leica now lists it as archived.
applications: Cryo-CLEM targeting for cryo-FIB and cryo-ET

sources.title: Leica Microsystems: THUNDER Imager EM Cryo CLEM

name: EM Cryo CLEM

specs.Workflow: Cryo loading, fluorescence imaging, export of ROI coordinates to EM software

summary: Leica's earlier cryo fluorescence microscope for correlative light and electron microscopy, which records target coordinates for relocation in the EM. It was replaced by the THUNDER Imager EM Cryo CLEM.

name: First electron microscope
summary: Max Knoll and Ernst Ruska used two magnetic lenses in 1931 to form magnified electron images of a mesh grid, arguably the first electron microscope. By September 1933 an improved instrument exceeded the magnification of light microscopes on cotton fibres; Ruska shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physics for electron optics.

sources.title: Knoll & Ruska (1932) Das Elektronenmikroskop. Z. Physik 78:318-339

name: Stereoscan Mk1
summary: The first commercial scanning electron microscope, built on work by Charles Oatley's group at Cambridge; the first unit went to DuPont.

name: Scanning tunneling microscope

resolution.note: Typical STM: lateral features below 0.1 nm, depth resolution 0.01 nm

summary: Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer imaged surfaces with atomic resolution by scanning a sharp tip so close to the sample that electrons tunnel across the gap. It started the field of scanning probe microscopy and won them the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Atomic force microscope
summary: Binnig, Quate and Gerber measured the tiny force between a tip on a cantilever and a surface instead of a tunneling current, so non-conducting samples could be imaged too. The first commercial AFM followed in 1989.

sources.title: Binnig, Quate & Gerber (1986) Atomic force microscope. Phys Rev Lett 56:930

name: Vitrified-specimen cryo-EM
summary: Jacques Dubochet's group at EMBL showed in 1981 that thin films of water can be frozen so fast that they become glass-like (vitreous) rather than crystalline ice. In 1984 they imaged unstained viruses in such vitreous layers, establishing the sample preparation used in cryo-EM today.

sources.title: Adrian, Dubochet, Lepault & McDowall (1984) Cryo-electron microscopy of viruses. Nature 308:32-36

name: Bacteriorhodopsin structure by electron cryo-microscopy
manufacturer: Henderson lab (MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology)

resolution.note: 3.5 Å parallel to the membrane plane; lower perpendicular to it

summary: Richard Henderson and colleagues built an atomic model of the membrane protein bacteriorhodopsin from high-resolution electron cryo-microscopy of 2D crystals, building on Henderson and Unwin's 1975 low-resolution bacteriorhodopsin map. It showed that electron microscopy could reach near-atomic resolution for biological molecules.

sources.title: Henderson et al. (1990) Model for the structure of bacteriorhodopsin based on high-resolution electron cryo-microscopy. J Mol Biol 213:899-929

name: Single-particle image processing
manufacturer: Frank lab (Wadsworth Center, New York State Department of Health)
summary: From 1975 Joachim Frank developed computational methods to align and average many noisy images of individual, randomly oriented molecules into a 3D structure, the basis of single-particle cryo-EM. He shared the 2017 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Dubochet and Henderson.

name: Elmiskop I

specs.Notable feature: First electron microscope with a double condenser, allowing routine electron diffraction

summary: Siemens transmission electron microscope developed after the war with Ernst Ruska's involvement; its double condenser made it a worldwide workhorse for a decade. Dates of 1954 to 1956 appear in different sources.
